_comment: Reviewed ceilings for the acceptance-state debt counters (#31). Each counter is a way a completion claim can outrun its evidence, and each may only go down: a rise is a new contradiction entering the repository, and a fall that has not been banked is slack a later regression could spend. Enforced by scripts/check-ac-state.py --ratchet, which refuses to compare across measurement modes -- without --run-tests no criterion can reach the passing rung, so the counters mean something different. Bank a reviewed improvement with --ratchet --bank and read the diff; never hand-edit a number to match a delta. Three counters added by #164 check the ADR -> spec -> AC chain in the ABSENT direction: specs_implementing_nothing (a spec naming no ADR -- `implements: []` is valid front matter, so the registry's dangling-reference check never saw it), adrs_without_implementing_spec (a decision taken -- Accepted or Implemented -- that no spec implements and that carries no criteria of its own; Proposed is excluded because a decision not yet made cannot be owed an implementation), and specs_declaring_no_criteria (no criteria AND no acceptance heading, split out of specs_awaiting_retrofit so "there are none" stops hiding inside "there are none yet"; a spec may opt out with an `<!-- ac-state: non-measurable - reason -->` marker, which is mandatory-reason and visible in the diff). Together these turn "specs map to ADRs" from "specs do not MIS-map to ADRs" into the claim a green build is actually read as supporting.
